recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is recommended for this issue unless BR&R wants an editorial-only grammar cleanup outside this reconciliation workflow.
issue_request: FHIR-31795 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R clarification request asking what differs between PackagedProductDefinition.identifier and PackagedProductDefinition.package.identifier and what a Data Carrier Identifier is. The resolution said the top-level identifier is for the whole package, the child package identifier is for packaging parts, and a Data Carrier Identifier is the GS1 bar code.
initial_application: The request was applied before this reconciliation. Commit 8f276af0294e5a576ebd983b58659aa54899dff2 changed the generic PackagedProductDefinition.identifier and PackagedProductDefinition.package.identifier wording to whole-package and packaging-part descriptions for FHIR#31795/FHIR#31796, and c58270261982846561c4e2c2a7612e2b1f660b55 synced the same wording from R4B for FHIR#31795. Later commits 09e9fd4d7caabbd76b12d2c73f26a9adf5c3ab22 and 41d2b22c8d91836f8c43576c245312a37a8c9bfe preserved the distinction while refining the text.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes PackagedProductDefinition in the current build and marks it normative and approved. FHIR-29692 later renamed PackagedProductDefinition.package to PackagedProductDefinition.packaging, so the seed's .package.identifier target is now PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.identifier. FHIR-31796 is a same-change-family issue already represented on the combined branch, and FHIR-29783 later recorded that the PackagedProductDefinition identifier wording had already been updated. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source change. The current StructureDefinition already says PackagedProductDefinition.identifier is a unique identifier for the package as a whole and not the contents, while PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.identifier is specific to a particular part of the packaging and may include a Data Carrier Identifier, a GS1 barcode.
